avis.comment: Purely theoretical paper (Reproducibility Statement: no experiments or datasets), so theory_only / not_applicable / no domains is correct and a null GPU-hour reference is plausible. The problem statement keeps to background and prior work and poses the open questions (role of depth and readouts, adequacy of standard separation for equivariant networks, saturation with depth) as questions without stating answers. All quotes check out verbatim; targets are recast sensibly for a theory paper.

targets.comment: Quote is verbatim (Sec. 5.2); recovering known special cases (Segol-Lipman set networks, classical MLP universality listed in Prior Work 1) is a sound sanity check for any general characterization.
Quote verbatim from the introduction (prior result of Pacini et al. 2025); checking against the same-separation/different-approximation counterexample is a reasonable control. Overlaps with S2.
Quote verbatim (Sec. 3.3); proving the necessity direction alongside density is required for any exact characterization.

Quote verbatim (Example 3); testing the separation notion on an explicitly computable architecture (width-1 convolutions under S_n) is well supported, though it closely mirrors the paper's own counterexample.
Quote verbatim (Sec. 5.2); comparing with/without readout at matched separation follows the problem's question on the role of readouts and Prior Work 6.
Quote matches Sec. 4 (escaped backslashes decode to the markdown text); this is Theorem 1, the core invariant result.
Quote verbatim from the introduction; entry-wise separation via projections onto output coordinates is the paper's key equivariant idea.
Quote verbatim (Theorem 2); depth stabilization plus width-1 conv readout (Theorem 3) and finite-depth saturation (Corollary 1) are correctly described.
Quote verbatim (Sec. 5); the paper shows via Example 3 that global separation fails to characterize equivariant universality classes.
Quote verbatim from the introduction; the failure is a prior result (Pacini et al. 2025) that the paper restates and builds on, so acceptable though largely redundant with C2.
